No explicit rationale found for these individual removals in the supplied body, commits, or plans.

A five-row resource derivation table, lower-constrained-memory selection assertions, and a literal 250 ms constant assertion. The local calculator itself is deleted too.
Already elsewhere

A new resource test uses 17 ms and tiny distinct RSS thresholds to observe injection. The existing 250 ms sampling behavior test remains.

The healthy-startup test still holds readiness behind a gate and asserts it remains pending. Its formerly supplied startupTimeoutMs: 5 is removed as the option disappears. The built-process test expects Windows to retain the ready record until a caller removes it, without a termination log. POSIX expects child-side cleanup and one log. This local run exercised macOS only.

HOW THIS PAGE WAS MADE

Source readings, plus bounded local execution
Claims and reasons

Compared PR bodies and commits with the exact bundle diffs, base/head tests and implementations, and the architecture, policy and follow-up specs. Earlier experiments were ignored. Reasons are attributed; test reach is our reading of the actual setup and assertions.

Deletion accounting

Tracked renamed files before interpreting deletions. Looked for replacement witnesses when assertions or fixtures changed. A replacement is shown with its new boundary, rather than treated as interchangeable with the old test.

Execution limits

Selected existing tests ran against supplied head builds on macOS 15 / Node 22.12.0. The package test typecheck ran for #148. This is not a full CI run; CLI end-to-end suites and Windows execution were not run for this experiment.

The retry probe is a separate reproduction of the new #131 socket scenario against supplied base/head builds. It creates temporary sockets/spools and records events; it does not launch a daemon or execute a CLI command. Tracked worktree status was clean before and after the selected checks.

Erase entries before project release can settle

Release synchronously empties all six caches, then starts and awaits project release. Old cached entries are unavailable while release is pending or rejecting. Clearing does not block new queries: a query may refill a cache during the wait.

MECHANISM

Move completion to the far side of project release

Backend release now waits for project release and propagates its rejection; previously it could resolve while project release was pending. The PR names this API change while also claiming failure behavior is preserved. It gives no reason reconciling those two claims.

UNEXPLAINEDAn awaited backend barrier is documented, but no rationale was found for this caller-observable timing/rejection change within a preservation-only refactor.
